programme.desc: What if we all decided to buy less and buy better? In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast, we had the privilege of sitting down with fair-fashion campaigner, author, and thought-leader Aja Barber to learn about her own journey and career in the fashion and media industries, to touch on the real cost of fast fashion and overconsumption, and the joy that comes with buying less and buying better. In a world where we are taught to senselessly and unceasingly ‘BUY BUY BUY!’, overcoming overconsumption is as simple as: loving what we already have, fixing that which is broken, borrowing that which we only need for a short time, and seeking out secondhand as the first option when we want or need something new.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.sub-title: Restore Nature & Bring Back Joy with Christabel Reed of Earthed
programme.desc: WE ALL NEED NATURE SKILLS. For millennia, knowledge and skillsets like tending land, saving seeds, maintaining soil health, and working within a community agricultural framework were passed down from generation to generation. In the midst of the industrial revolution, the creation of the 40-hour work week, and rapidly urbanising cities that don’t prioritise green spaces, these vital skills that connect us to the land are largely unknown to most in the West. In this episode of The Inspire Action Podcast, Ciara sits down with Christabel Reed, co-founder of platforms Advaya and Earthed. While Advaya centres around sharing knowledge and wisdom about mythology, ecology, and spirituality, Earthed offers free, online nature skills courses that aim to reconnect people with nature by getting them directly involved with it. Ciara and Christabel discuss ecological responsibility, bringing joy back to regeneration, land stewardship, barriers to entry, how our current systems can block our ability to be in nature as much as we need to be, and how everyone can work to restore our Earth.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.sub-title: Super Seaweed Solving the Plastic Problem (with Pierre Paslier, Notpla)
programme.desc: SUPER SEAWEED TO THE RESCUE! No, this seaweed hasn’t been genetically modified to fight off mutants–it’s just working to combat the plastic crisis, of course! One of the most dire issues our world today faces is the overproduction and overconsumption of plastic. With waste streams ill-equipped to handle the volume and varying types of plastic, as much as 23 million metric tonnes of plastic end up in our world’s waterways each year! Not only is this plastic choking marine life and ecosystems, but it’s also having devastating impacts on human health, communities, and economies. Founded in 2014, Notpla is on a mission to eliminate single-use plastic packaging with their innovative seaweed-based product. Their seaweed packaging is entirely biodegradable, organic, and made from seaweed harvested for industrial use (no fishy habitat destruction here!) In this episode, Ciara and Pierre discuss the plastic crisis, Notpla’s incredible 2022 Earthshot Prize win, how their work is eliminating tens of millions of pieces of single-use plastic across Europe and the UK, their future ambitions to use their product to better our world.

programme.title: Going Green: Green Green World
programme.sub-title: Every Building in 2050 Will Be Covered in MOSS!
programme.desc: This is why moss is the future of sustainable architecture! Alive Labs in London, are growing moss panels that can be installed in cities to help remove air pollution, suck up carbon dioxide, regulate the temperature and absorb rainwater! Moss’ potential has not been fully harnessed in architecture until now. It’s fire-resistant due to the modular shape, requires very little maintenance and the shapes can be customised to create moss artwork! The surrounding material is also the world's first bio receptive concrete made from fully organic materials. Building facades offer so much opportunity to reintroduce biodiversity into cities. This is a practical, easy to install solution, which we hope to see in cities around the world soon.

programme.title: Spook Town
programme.desc: Dry Gulch Trading Post owner Kurt Fabian advances money on mortgages to the local settlers to finance an irrigation program. Three Texas Rangers, Tex Wyatt, Jim Steele and Panhandle Perkins transport the money in a strong box which they place in the Wells Fargo safe as agent Sam Benson assures them that he is the only one who knows the safe combination. Fabian conspires with Bill Gunner, Breed Crocker and Trigger Booth to steal the money and they fail, but Fabian gets it on his own. Benson is arrested, and a committee of citizens, led by Oscar Perrin accuse Captain Wyatt and the Rangers of carelessness and request the resignation of the Captain if the money is not recovered. Fabian owns the abandoned ghost town of "Mystic", and Gunner, Crocker and Booth take him there to force him to tell where he has hidden the money, They shoot at his feet to intimidate him and he dies from fright and shock. Tex, Jim and Panhandle are also searching the town and they find Fabian's body. Benson tells Lucy Warren that the money may be hidden in the old Wells Fargo office in Mystic and they go there and find the strongbox. Enter Gunner, Crocker and Booth. Enter the Rangers. Gunfight.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

Le fleuve evolue au cours de ce long voyage. L'apport de ses affluents, comme la Neste, l'Ariege, le Tarn et le Lot, modifie son visage. After his highly acclaimed debut film "Heile Welt" Jakob M. Erwa returns with his second feature film, the impressionistic psychodrama HOMESICK, which is also his first Berlin film.

programme.title: Clumsy Little Acts of Tenderness
programme.desc: A weekend dad wants to show his teenage daughter his love by taking her to a car wash, but instead of the car wash, they end up on a life-changing adventure at the supermarket, at the endless sanitary napkin display. They get "help" from an older lady who shares stories that might be just a bit too intimate.

programme.title: El Gran Inventario del Planeta: Sudáfrica

programme.title: Happiness Is a Warm Gun
programme.desc: What happens to Petra Kelly as Bastian's bullet enters her head until the moment the bullet lodges in her brain and Petra dies? She has a flash-forward to the present and awakens in the glass transit of an international airport. On her trip through this modern purgatory, Petra struggles to make sense of her shooting, together with Gert and other people from her life.

programme.title: Nation Estate
programme.desc: A vertical solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has been found for the political deadlock in the Middle East. Palestinians have their state in the form of a skyscraper. The building is called the NATION ESTATE. One colossal high-rise houses the entire Palestinian population – who are now finally living 'the high life'.

programme.title: Eglise du Saint-Sepulcre, Israel (Partie 1)
programme.desc: Une visite de l’eglise du Saint-Sepulcre, cœur de la ville sainte de Jerusalem. Situee dans le quartier chretien de Jerusalem, sur une petite place etroite, coincee entre les maisons de la vieille ville et au pied d’un minaret, l’eglise du Saint-Sepulcre se dresse au bout de la Via Dolorosa

programme.title: Amor Musical
programme.desc: Todo inicia cuando son transferidos a la escuela Jung San que recibe auspicio por parte de una fundación millonaria y poderosa. Como es de esperarse, los días escolares en esta escuela se convierte en una lucha sin fin. Cada día enfrentan el gran abismo entre el rico y el pobre. Ante la cruda realidad, en lo único que pueden confiar es en su música. Tocar con sus amigos es la única cosa que los mantiene vivos, al mismo tiempo, Su música los hace brillar por encima de los demás. “Amor Musical” es un drama musical como nunca antes visto; al mejor estilo y creado para el sentimiento punk.

programme.title: China Reverse
programme.desc: Film director Judith Benedikt embarks on a journey following first and second-generation immigrants from China in Austria, who are mainly stranded in Asian restaurants in the city and in the countryside. After half a century of migration, mainly in one direction, there is a new current flowing back to the East thanks to the economic boom in China.

programme.title: El Gran Inventario del Planeta: Polinesia de Gambier
programme.desc: The Explorers presenta una imagen no sólo bella, sino profundamente viva. En estas balsas de coral abandonadas por los volcanes, la vida se ha reinventado. De la nada, poco a poco, ha creado oasis, cada vez más ricos, con su propio equilibrio y tempo, el latido de los canales que riegan el atolón.

programme.title: Encuentros Que Generan Bienestar

programme.title: Eglise Sainte Anne et les Piscines de Bethesda, Israel
programme.desc: Situee au debut de la Via Dolorosa, l’eglise Sainte-Anne est le site traditionnel de la maison des grands-parents maternels de Jesus, Anne et Joachim, et du lieu de naissance de la Vierge Marie. Nichee au cœur des rues animees et des ruelles du quartier musulman, l’eglise Sainte-Anne, la mieux conservee des eglises croisees de Jerusalem, se distingue par sa tranquillite. Elle se trouve dans une cour entouree d’arbres et d’arbustes.

programme.desc: Everyday words and moments play out under the eyes of their visitor and and tension surrounding the ambiguity of their intimate friendship and their sexual encounters ensue. In the final act, in the wake of Monique’s absence, Maryam and Frida try to continue with their routines while getting ready for a double date.

programme.title: Mont Tabor, Israel
programme.desc: Le mont Tabor est une colline historique dans le nord d’Israel, dominant la vallee de Jezreel et reconnue pour sa forme arrondie remarquable. Venere depuis des siecles, il possede une grande importance religieuse, notamment dans la tradition chretienne comme lieu de la Transfiguration, et offre des vues panoramiques impressionnantes sur le paysage environnant.

programme.title: Armonia Vintage
programme.desc: Gaspar y Majo son dos viajeros apasionados por descubrir el mundo sin prisa. A traves de sus recuerdos y experiencias, reviven un viaje realizado anos atras por el Caribe colombiano, las sierras y montanas de Colombia, Peru y Ecuador, compartiendo historias y lugares que invitan a conocer otras culturas y a encontrar bienestar en el camino.

programme.title: Kleptomami
programme.desc: Lucy (Rosalie Thomass) regularly shoplifts at the supermarket with her baby in the stroller. One day she is confronted by the store detective and reveals her secret to him. Lucy is tired of pretending to be the perfect mother. "She is torn between her own aspirations and the reality in which they find themselves after the birth of their child." (Director's comment - Pola Beck).

programme.desc: Buzzing with lust for adventure, a musician from Dublin and his band move to Berlin. Oisin leaves behind the weight of losing his mother, and anger towards his absent father. Oisin meets Sabine, a pretty Berliner who shows him the city's secret places: cool parks, deserted subway stations, skinny dipping lakes in the countryside.

programme.title: Swimmers
programme.desc: The controversial Soviet physicist Boris Zolotov left science to start a movement. He has gathered hundreds of disciples around him. Like many in the group, young Ekaterina was led there by many unanswered questions. Together with Boris Zolotov, she takes part in hour-long swimming rituals and night-time theater performances and discusses concepts of happiness in today´s Russia.

programme.title: Kursi, Parc National, Israel
programme.desc: Le parc national de Kursi en Israel est un site archeologique et historique situe sur la rive est de la mer de Galilee. Il conserve les vestiges d’un monastere et d’une eglise byzantins, traditionnellement consideres comme le lieu du miracle des porcs de Geraseens par Jesus, et offre aux visiteurs des vues panoramiques, des mosaïques anciennes et un aperçu de l’histoire chretienne ancienne.

programme.desc: Der chinesische Autohersteller Nio geht das Thema "E-Auto laden" anders an als die Konkurrenz. In sogenannten Battery-Swap-Stations soll der Akku innerhalb von nur fünf Minuten gewechselt werden. Ist das die Zukunft der Elektromobilität? Alexander Bloch testet die Anlage und klärt die 9 größten Irrtümer zum Akkuwechsel beim E-Auto.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Golf 7
programme.desc: Der VW Golf 7 ist eines der meistverkauften und beliebtesten Modelle des Volkswagenkonzerns. Worauf man beim Kauf eines gebrauchten Golf 7 achten muss erklärt Alexander Bloch. Egal ob Probleme mit dem AGR-Ventil, dem DSG-Getriebe und Rost, die Schwachstellen und guten Seiten des Wolfsburger Dauerbrenners kommen hier zum Vorschein.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - 1.000.000 Kilometer
programme.desc: In der 100. Folge von Bloch erklärt kümmert sich Alex um das Thema Dauerläufer: Wie hält dein Auto ewig? Im Mittelpunkt steht ein Lexus LS400 mit einer Million Kilometer auf der Uhr. Wie fährt sich so ein Kilometerfresser eigentlich? Und was muss man tun, damit das eigene Auto auch das Zeug zum Dauerläufer hat? Alex Bloch erklärt euch 10 wichtige Regeln - das wird gut!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - E-Autos 2023
programme.desc: Die Lieferzeiten bei Elektroautos sind lang. Doch zumindest wird 2023 die Auswahl deutlich größer. Besonders die chinesischen Hersteller wollen angreifen und zeigen zahlreiche Neuheiten. Aber auch die deutschen Produzenten legen nach. Alexander Bloch zeigt seine 10 Highlights für das Jahr 2023. Hier seht ihr seine Favoriten.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Sicherheits-Irrtümer
programme.desc: Welche Autos sind am sichersten? Welche Aussagekraft haben Crashtests überhaupt? Warum spielt die Farbe eines Autos in der Unfallstatistik eine Rolle? Die Antwort auf diese Fragen und weitere spannende Informationen rund um das Thema Verkehrssicherheit gibt es in dieser Folge Bloch erklärt. Zudem findet Alexander Bloch unter den Testdummies einen neuen Freund: Thor!

programme.desc: Neuauflage des RC-Duells zwischen Alex Bloch und Lance David Arnold. Auf der Strecke des RCRT Duisburg geht es heute nicht um Schnelligkeit, sondern genaues fahren. Wer schafft den Trail-Parcous fehlerfrei mit seinem Absima Sherpa?

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Fendt 1050 Vario-Teil 2
programme.desc: Unter der Motorhaube des größten Standard-Traktor der Welt brummt ein 12,4-Liter-Reihensechszylinder-Diesel. Alexander Bloch fährt den Fendt 1050 Vario auf der Teststrecke Probe. Außerdem wartet eine kleine Herausforderung auf Alex, die viel Fingerspitzengefühl erfordert.

programme.title: Bloch spielt - Carrera Bahn
programme.desc: Sie ist einer der Spiele-Klassiker und darf in keinem Kinderzimmer eines echten Petrolheads fehlen: Die Carrera Bahn. Doch wie genau funktioniert die Bahn? Welche Technik wird eingesetzt? Und was kann man optimieren? Das alles und noch viel Mehr bei Bloch spielt.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Fendt 1050 Vario-Teil 1
programme.desc: Fendt 1050 Vario: der stärkste Standard-Traktor der Welt! Er leistet beachtliche 517 PS und 2.420 Newtonmeter Drehmoment. Wie der Gigant produziert wird und welche technischen Raffinessen er zu bieten hat, schaut sich Alexander Bloch in den heiligen Hallen von Fendt an.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - VW ID.7 Effizienzcheck (Teil 1)
programme.desc: Alex Bloch checkt den neuen VW ID.7 und weiht Euch in die Geheimnisse seines Antriebs ein. Die große Frage: Wie effizient kann ein Elektromotor sein und was kann man machen um ihn effizienter zu bekommen?

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - VW ID.7 Effizienzcheck (Teil 2)
programme.desc: Alex Bloch darf den VW ID.7 fahren und erklärt Euch im Detail, was die neue vollelektrische Limousine von Volkswagen kann.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - 8 Todsünden beim Winterreifen-Wechsel
programme.desc: Noch sind die Temperaturen mild, doch so langsam sollte der Wechsel auf Winterreifen erfolgen. Oder setzt ihr auf Allwetter-Reifen? Alex Bloch klärt die 8 Todsünden beim Wechsel auf wintertaugliche Reifen.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Die 5 größten Fehler bei VW unter Diess
programme.desc: Ob Qualität oder Bedienung: In verschiedenen einstigen Paradedisziplinen hat VW den Anschluss an die Konkurrenz verloren. Mit dafür verantwortlich: Herbert Diess. Als Vorstandsvorsitzender der Volkswagen AG hat er den Konzern ins Elektro-Auto-Zeitalter geführt. Dabei hat er vieles angeschoben, aber auch einige Baustellen hinterlassen. Alex Bloch beleuchtet die Fehler unter Diess und welche Baustellen VW in Zukunft angehen muss.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Die 10 Gebote des guten Tunings: SO tunt ihr richtig!
programme.desc: Tuning geht über rein äußerliche Veränderungen hinaus. Es handelt sich um eine Kombination von Modifikationen, die nicht nur die Optik, sondern auch das Fahrverhalten eines Fahrzeugs verbessern sollen. Das Ziel: eine ausgewogene und beherrschbare Performance. Alexander Bloch zeigt, worauf es beim Tuning ankommt am Beispiel des Steeda Mustang Q767 Mach 1.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Warum Rennwagen für die Zukunft wichtig sind
programme.desc: Alexander Bloch besucht das VDI-Racing-Camp powered by norelem und erklärt 5 Gründe, wieso die Formula Student wichtig für die Zukunft des Autos ist.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Performance Tesla
programme.desc: Elon Musk und Tesla haben in der Vergangenheit schon so manche Leistungsversprechen abgegeben, bei denen einem regelrecht schwindelig wird. Einige davon sind eingetreten, andere aber eben nicht. Im zweiten Teil zu Tesla-Versprechungen nimmt Alex die Performance Angaben ganz genau unter die Lupe. Er erklärt, warum manche Angaben zu Leistung, Beschleunigung und Rennstreckenperformance mit Vorsicht zu genießen sind.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Verbrenner - Elektro
programme.desc: Der Verbrennungsmotor wird auf den Straßen Stück für Stück vom Elektromotor abgelöst. Dennoch sind Diesel und Benziner noch immer ein wichtiger Bestandteil der Mobilität. Doch wie steht es um die Effizienz der Verbrennungsmotoren? Alexander Bloch erklärt die 5 größten Effizienz-Irrtümer.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Getriebeirrtümer
programme.desc: Getriebe sind aus Autos nicht wegzudenken: Doch es gibt viele Irrtümer zu Getrieben, egal ob Schalter oder Automatik. Alex klärt die wichtigsten Irrtümer

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Rekuperation
programme.desc: Was bringt Bremsenergie-Rückgewinnung wirklich? Um diese Frage zu beantworten, ist Alexander Bloch zur Silvretta Hochalpen-Straße gereist und hat den großen Test gemacht. Mit dabei: Der 761-PS-Sportler Porsche Taycan Turbo S und der kleine Fiat 500e. Die Ergebnisse sind überraschend!

programme.title: Ice 2020 - Parte 2
programme.desc: E ‘il 2020. I risultati di uno scienziato ambientale, il Professor Thom Archer suggeriscono che Halo, l’impresa di perforazione della società energetica sul ghiacciaio della Groenlandia ne stanno causando lo scioglimento. Gli avvertimenti di Archer vengono ignorati, così si dirige verso l’Artico per trovare prove inconfutabili. Al suo arrivo, si rende conto che l’umanità è in pericolo immediato, e corre a casa per salvare la sua famiglia. Il ghiacciaio collassa, con conseguenze devastanti...

programme.title: 40 Days And Nights - Apocalisse Finale
programme.desc: Se un imponente spostamento tettonico causasse uno tsunami di proporzioni enormi, quale sarebbe l'unica soluzione? Recuperare l'insegnamento di Noè e della sua arca e costruire un'enorme nave capace di contenere solo cinquantamila persone, più il DNA di tutte le specie esistenti al mondo, cercando così di salvarle da una tempesta apocalittica.

programme.title: Empire Of The Sharks
programme.desc: Adrenalinico sci-fi scritto e diretto da Mark Atkins (Jurassic School) e sequel di Planet of the Sharks. In un futuro dove il 98% della superficie terrestre è sott’acqua, uno spietato signore della guerra governa grazie al suo esercito di super squali. Solo una ragazza con il potere psichico di comunicare con gli squali tenterà di opporsi, per sconfiggere il tiranno e liberare la sua gente.

programme.title: 2012: Il Giorno Del Giudizio
programme.desc: 21 dicembre 2012. Quattro stranieri in viaggio si ritrovano ai piedi di un antico tempio inesplorato nel cuore del Messico. Per i Maya è l'ultimo giorno del calendario, per gli scienziati della Nasa è una catastrofica inversione dei poli magnetici della terra. Per l'umanità è il giorno del giudizio. L'apocalisse è vicina.

programme.title: Un Natale Di Ghiaccio
programme.desc: Action movie ambientato tra i ghiacci dell’Alaska con Brendan Fehr e Jodelle Ferland. Siamo alla Vigilia di Natale e l’idillio delle feste viene bruscamente interrotto quando i ghiacciai, sciogliendosi, iniziano a rilasciare grandi quantità di metano liquido che, se non fermato, rischia di far esplodere l'intero pianeta.

programme.title: Apocalypse Pompeii
programme.desc: Apocalypse Pompeii

programme.title: Alien Convergence
programme.desc: Una squadra, composta da persone con disabilità fisiche, sviluppa un rivoluzionario progetto per pilotare gli aerei da combattimento attraverso un collegamento neurale. Quando dalla NASA scoprono che qualcosa sta per entrare nell'atmosfera, tale progetto viene messo in atto per respingere un'invasione aliena.

programme.title: The Recall - L'invasione
programme.desc: Charlie (RJ Mitte) si unisce ai suoi amici durante un weekend, in una cabina sul lago. Quella notte, un raggio di luce ultraterrena spunta giù dal cielo e rapisce gran parte del gruppo, portandolo sulla nave madre. I due superstiti, Charlie e Annie, devono fare affidamento su un eccentrico e misterioso cacciatore locale (Wesley Snipes), che sembra avere già esperienze dell'attacco.

programme.title: Absolon: Virus Mortale
programme.desc: Un virus ha infettato l'intera umanità e l'Absolon è un farmaco indispensabile per sopravvivere. Un agente di polizia inizia a indagare sull'omicidio di uno scienziato che stava lavorando a un antidoto contro il virus, arrivando a scoprire una cospirazione. Da quel momento diviene il bersaglio della società che monopolizza l'Absolon.

programme.title: Icetastrophe
programme.desc: Un meteorite entra nell'atmosfera terrestre e si spezza a metà. Un pezzo colpisce il centro di Lennox, negli Stati Uniti, e subito dopo l'area circostante inizia a congelarsi; l'altro ha creato una nuova zona tropicale. L' umanità potrebbe salvarsi solo con il ricongiungimento delle due metà.

programme.title: Age Of Dinosaurs
programme.desc: Una società di biotecnologie riporta in vita alcuni dinosauri grazie a una rivoluzionaria tecnologia di rigenerazione della pelle. Quando però le creature preistoriche riescono a scappare da una mostra e a seminare il panico in tutta Los Angeles, un ex pompiere deve riuscire a salvare la figlia adolescente dal caos da loro provocato.

programme.title: 2025: Armageddon
programme.desc: Una razza aliena attacca la Terra utilizzando creature giganti e catastrofi naturali ispirate ai film trasmessi dal canale The Asylum's Movie Channel, che ha raggiunto il loro pianeta. Un gruppo di eroi improbabili deve unire le forze per fermare la distruzione e salvare il mondo da una catastrofe imminente.

programme.title: Proof over Promise: Insights on Real-World AI Adoption
programme.desc: At a moment when artificial intelligence is moving beyond hype into measurable impact, the key question is no longer what AI can do—but how it delivers at scale. From manufacturing floors to energy systems, the race is on to turn promise into proof. As home to one of the fastest-moving AI deployment environments, how is China translating policy into large-scale industrial application? Join BizTalk as we team up with the World Economic Forum, bringing together leaders from WEF, CATL, and Schneider Electric to explore how AI is being driven by real business needs, and how it’s redefining the future of intelligent manufacturing.

programme.title: Global business voices on China-US trade relations
programme.desc: China-US relations draws global attention, the global business community is closely watching what US President Donald Trump's visit to China means for trade, investment and market confidence. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN’s Lincoln Humphries sits down with Fred Teng, president of the AmericaChina Public Affairs Institute, Chris Torrens, chairman of the British Chamber of Commerce in China, and Oliver Oehms, executive director and board member of the German Chamber of Commerce in China – North China; exploring investment sentiment, business trends and why China-US cooperation still matters in an uncertain global economy.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: Live: Beyond the buzz: What do young Americans really think about China-US relations?
programme.desc: What happens when young Americans experience China beyond the headlines? Join CGTN for a candid conversation with US creators and students living in China as they share firsthand perspectives on daily life, consumer trends, innovation, and how these experiences are reshaping their understanding of China's economic dynamism and China-US connections.

programme.title: Around China: Explore Lijiang's vibrant nighttime economy with Naxi culture
programme.desc: In recent years, Lijiang, Yunnan Province, has been leveraging its unique local resources to enrich and elevate its nighttime economy. By promoting activities such as nighttime dining, scenic views, and evening performances, Lijiang has unleashed vibrant consumer energy, attracting a growing number of tourists. Join CGTN Reporter Zhu Zhu to immerse in the Naxi ethnic wear, taking part in a bonfire party at Sifang Street, and explore Lijiang’s nighttime economy firsthand!

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: Live: Beyond the buzz: What do young Americans really think about China-US relations?
programme.desc: What happens when young Americans experience China beyond the headlines? Join CGTN for a candid conversation with US creators and students living in China as they share firsthand perspectives on daily life, consumer trends, innovation, and how these experiences are reshaping their understanding of China's economic dynamism and China-US connections.

programme.title: Around China: Explore Lijiang's vibrant nighttime economy with Naxi culture
programme.desc: In recent years, Lijiang, Yunnan Province, has been leveraging its unique local resources to enrich and elevate its nighttime economy. By promoting activities such as nighttime dining, scenic views, and evening performances, Lijiang has unleashed vibrant consumer energy, attracting a growing number of tourists. Join CGTN Reporter Zhu Zhu to immerse in the Naxi ethnic wear, taking part in a bonfire party at Sifang Street, and explore Lijiang’s nighttime economy firsthand!

programme.title: Proof over Promise: Insights on Real-World AI Adoption

programme.desc: China-US relations draws global attention, the global business community is closely watching what US President Donald Trump's visit to China means for trade, investment and market confidence. programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night"

programme.title: Foodwise: Changsha
programme.desc: In this episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May embark on a journey to Changsha in Hunan Province.?They taste their way through the local cuisine, discover the city's latest art and fashion trends, and find out why this place is one of China's "influencer hotspots", attracting millions of domestic and foreign tourists each year.

programme.title: Foodwise：Qingdao
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Qingdao, China's beer mecca by the sea. With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more!

programme.title: A Vibe of the Village: The Beat of Xiangxi Drums
programme.desc: Experience the vibrant power of Xiangxi Drum Dance. This program delves into the heart of Tujia and Miao cultures, showcasing the rhythmic beats and spirited performances that have echoed through West Hunan's mountains for centuries. Discover the stories, traditions, and raw energy of this captivating folk art.

programme.title: Young dancer of Batang melody
programme.desc: Tibetan girl Tashi Badro from Batang, Ganzi, Sichuan has learned how to do the Xianzi dance both from her mom and a school program. Batang Xianzi is a unique folk dance of the Tibetan ethnic group with a history spanning over 1,000 years on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. In order to keep the Tibetan tradition alive, Badro’s school has offered the dance as a cultural activity. Badro said dancing with her classmates is the happiest moment of her day. Watch the graceful movements of Badro and her peers performing the Xianzi dance.

programme.title: China Bound：Suzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji’s countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: Fujian’s Tulou – The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programme.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programme.title: Awakening Lion-1
programme.desc: Xingshi, or literally “awakened lion,” is a name for the southern style of the lion dance. Historically, it evolved from a court dance in the Tang Dynasty almost 1,200 years ago. With the southward migration of the population from the central plains, lion dance culture was introduced to the south. In the Ming Dynasty around 400 years ago, xingshi appeared in Guangdong and was then widely spread throughout southern China and even overseas. Lion dance has become a very important part of Chinese culture.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programme.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programme.title: Foodwise：Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.title: Guqin Music Art
programme.desc: The guqin is an instrument with a history of over 3,000 years. Yet in all that time, its design and sound have remained virtually unchanged. In 2003, the guqin and its music were proclaimed as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO. But how has this ancient instrument withstood the musical test of time? How do its slow, gentle melodies resonate in fast-paced modern China? In this episode of The Inheritors, we explore guqin music art’s history, development in modern days, and its future.

programme.title: Face-changing wonder boy
programme.desc: Face-changing is an ancient Chinese performance art that is a component of Sichuan opera. Hu Yibo, 13, learned the act from his grandfather and other experienced masters. Dressed in brightly-colored costumes and while changing from one mask to another in just the blink of an eye, Yibo skillfully swipes open a fan to hide his "magical" movements. As a young inheritor, he undertakes daily training to perfect his skill set in the hope of becoming a master one day.

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous "mala" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon – one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous "mala" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: Face-changing wonder boy
programme.desc: Face-changing is an ancient Chinese performance art that is a component of Sichuan opera. Hu Yibo, 13, learned the act from his grandfather and other experienced masters. Dressed in brightly-colored costumes and while changing from one mask to another in just the blink of an eye, Yibo skillfully swipes open a fan to hide his "magical" movements. As a young inheritor, he undertakes daily training to perfect his skill set in the hope of becoming a master one day.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon – one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programme.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programme.title: Presentimientos
programme.desc: Un largo viaje a través de los miedos y las esperanzas de una madre novata desde un terrible e inesperado suceso que la ayudará a profundizar y enfrentar sus secretos más oscuros.

programme.title: Un amor de película
programme.desc: Comedia romantica acerca de un director de cine que es engañado por su productor y distribuidor.

programme.title: Amalia
programme.desc: Una mujer se obsesiona con la amante de su ex amante.

programme.title: 6 Impactos
programme.desc: Un traficante roba a su patrón para salvar a su hijo.

programme.title: La Boleta
programme.desc: La vida de Pablo es una serie de eventos desafortunados. Después de un intento de suicidio fallido, tiene un sueño con números ganadores de lotería. Sin embargo, cuando va a comprar un billete, es asaltado. Sin dejarse desanimar, Pablo cree que los números aún serán ganadores y persigue a los ladrones por un barrio pobre.

programme.title: Cobardes
programme.desc: Gaby, un pelirrojo de 14 ańos en Barcelona, sufre constantes robos y palizas a manos de Guille y su despiadada pandilla, quienes lo apodan "Zanahoria". Incapaz de compartir su sufrimiento con sus padres, siempre ocupados con sus trabajos, Gaby se encierra en sí mismo mientras el bullying se intensifica. La madre de Guille encuentra un video violento en el móvil de su hijo y, aunque lo borra, Guille niega todo y se presenta como víctima ante el psicólogo escolar. La historia da un giro inesperado cuando el dueńo de la pizzería favorita de Gaby, un mafioso secreto, podría tener una pista que cambiará radicalmente las cosas. La situación se complica aún más cuando los padres de los involucrados, absortos en sus propios problemas, no logran percibir la magnitud del sufrimiento de Gaby, dejándolo cada vez más aislado y vulnerable.

programme.title: Aurelia la Texana
programme.desc: Aurelia busca venganza por la muerte de su madre.

programme.title: Chuecatown
programme.desc: Víctor es un agente inmobiliario en el barrio de Chueca en Madrid. Pero esconde un terrible secreto; sus apartamentos se ponen a la venta cuando asesina a las ancianas propietarias y disfraza el crimen como suicidio.
